title: Conversations with Goddard: Jody Davis
description: Jody Davis, Deputy Payload Systems Engineer for the Wide Field Infrared Survey Telescope (WFIRST), inspires and uplifts the world. Davis supports the design, development, build and test of the WFIRST payload including collaborating with our many WFIRST partners especially about critical interfaces. She thrives on challenges – from never-done-before engineering feats, to being a pilot, climbing Kilimanjaro, doing STEM outreach in South Africa and Tanzania and running marathons on each continent.
via: the NASA Image and Video Library

transcript.text: I actually didn't know what an engineer really was until I was about 13 years old.
I had always been interested in space, planets, you know, our solar system and stars.
And I was also interested in design.
So then I watched the movie Apollo 13 and I learned what aerospace engineering was
and how that was a beautiful marriage of my love of space and my love of design.
And then I had something to shoot for and I fell in love with NASA.
So I'm the deputy payload systems engineer on W-First at Goddard.
So my education background, I went to Embry Riddle, Aeronautical University,
and I got my bachelor's in aerospace engineering.
Then I went on to grad school at UVA and got a master's in aerospace and mechanical engineering.
Before all of that, I fell in love with flying.
I was in high school. Right about the time that I was learning to drive, I started flying.
Before school, I would go fly, get my hours in, and then after school, I would work at a
hair salon to actually pay for my flying lessons.
And I ended up getting my pilot's license my senior year of high school.
I like to do STEM outreach a lot and at one point I was like, you know what,
I really would love to do international STEM outreach.
I found a nonprofit organization in Tanzania called Project Inspire.
And I went out and I talked about NASA with them for two and a half weeks.
I plan to go back about every other year. I like challenges.
And I came up with this idea once I started running marathons and I want to run a marathon
on every continent before I'm 50. The last one I ran was in Iceland.
And then the next one that I have planned is to run the Mount Fuji Marathon in Japan.
Yes, I did climb Kilimanjaro. I still can't believe it.
It's a 19,300 foot peak. It was the hardest thing I've ever done.
And getting to the top, you're kind of almost euphoric.
What I enjoy most about working at Goddard is the people.
To tie it all together, we have a very capable hard-working team.
And I crave that highly collaborative environment where even as issues crop up,
you know that you can pull your team together and find the right answer.
My sixth word memoir is she inspired and uplifted the world.
